MlxModules.ModuleIdentity: Each source file is a module namespace.
MlxModules.GlobalInitialization: Global const and var initializers must be comptime evaluable. There are no hidden runtime global constructors.
MlxModules.GlobalAddresses: The address of a function, of a string literal's bytes, of another global or of an element or field of one is a constant a var's initializer may hold, alone or inside an array or struct literal. A var's bytes are static data at one address; the address words in them are filled in before main, as a loader's relocation would fill them: no code of the program runs for it.
MlxModules.Destructors: There are no general destructors. @noncopy aggregates may opt into lexical automatic deinitialization through fn deinit(self: *Self) -> void; all other cleanup remains explicit.
MlxModules.CircularImports: Allowed only if declaration resolution does not require cyclic CTFE evaluation.
MlxModules.TypesAcrossImportRings: Modules that import one another may name one another's types in their own: a struct of one with a pointer to a struct of the other and that one with a pointer back, a struct of one inside a struct of the other. A declaration of a module whose turn has not come is resolved when it is named, in its own module; a struct, union or enum still being resolved is the type it will be wherever a pointer to it is enough. Two aggregates that hold one another by value have no layout, in one module or in two.
